title: Add pcb_differential_pair_phase_skew element
description: Adds pcb_differential_pair_phase_skew element to store phase skew along routed differential pairs for accurate rendering in KiCad.
body:
Adds `pcb_differential_pair_phase_skew`. It stores phase skew along a routed differential pair so core can compute it once and the renderers only draw it. Phase skew is the value KiCad's differential pair phase skew tool shows.

It isn't stacked on anything. The renderer overlays (circuit-to-canvas #333, circuit-json-webgpu #116) currently compute phase skew themselves through `circuit-json-to-differential-pair-phase-skew`. Once core writes this element, they'll read it instead and drop that dependency.

### What is stored

There is one element per routed pair whose traces run together somewhere:

- The element has `source_bus_id`, `positive_trace` and `negative_trace`, plus an optional `subcircuit_id`.
- Each trace has its `pcb_trace_id` and its `segments`.
- Each segment has `start`, `end`, `layer` and `width`, plus `start_length_difference_mm` and `end_length_difference_mm`. Phase skew changes linearly between the two ends. Each value is how much longer this trace is than the other trace of the pair up to that point, in mm. The positive trace stores positive minus negative, and the negative trace stores negative minus positive, so the two show opposite signs at the same spot (same as KiCad).

Unknown phase skew is shown by leaving copper uncovered, not by a missing field, so nobody can read an absent value as 0. A pair that never runs together gets no element.

### Rejected by the schema

Each rule has its own test.

- Both sides pointing at the same `pcb_trace`
- A blank `source_bus_id` or `pcb_trace_id`
- A trace with no segments
- A segment with zero length or `width <= 0`
- Non-finite numbers
- A segment whose phase skew changes sign. Core splits these at zero, so renderers can draw each segment as an exact two-stop gradient (white to blue, or white to red).

### Left out on purpose

- **Colour scales and the pair's largest skew:** these come from the segment ends.
- **End-to-end length difference:** this comes from the two `pcb_trace`s.
- **`max_length_skew`:** this is already on `source_bus`.
- **Colours:** these are renderer options.

### New concepts

- **Phase skew:** at each point where the positive and negative traces run side by side, how much longer one is than the other up to that point, in mm. This is unlike length skew, which only compares the two ends.

There is no behaviour change: nothing writes this element yet.

The README gets only this element's section. Running `generate-docs` on main also adds about 400 lines of unrelated sections that are missing.

Checked locally: `bun test` (556 pass), `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint:zod`, `bun run check-snake-case`.

title: Render USB-C shell, cavity, and tongue from mechanical dimensions
description: Implements five vendor-neutral mechanical dimensions for USB-C connectors, enhancing the rendering of the shell, cavity, and tongue based on specified measurements.
body:
Implements the five vendor-neutral mechanical dimensions released in @tscircuit/footprinter 0.0.452 (https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/pull/1024). Distances are measured from the front lip of the USB-C shell. The rear insulator starts at the authored cavity depth, and the tongue and contacts follow the requested setback and thickness.

```text
usbcmidmount16_shelldepth7.3mm_shellwall0.30mm_cavitydepth4mm_tonguesetback0.30mm_tonguethickness0.62mm
```

The legacy body remains available when dimensions are omitted. The renderer reads validated millimetre values directly from Footprinter’s USB-C schema. Its minimum peer version is 0.0.452.

Using the existing board connector's pad and tab coordinates, the five added dimensions improve sampled volume IoU with its reference model from 44.65% to 77.72% on a 256 × 256 grid. This is below the 80% model-match threshold. The board footprint is independent of this renderer change.

Verified the individual measurements, contact overlap, peg/tail/tab positions and invalid combinations. The 10 USB-C geometry and snapshot tests, package build, type check and format check pass. The four-view snapshot exercises the React renderer and the measurement tests exercise the packaged vanilla renderer.

Footprinter also now registers `usba` and `usbmicro`. The missing-body list and two pad snapshots cover these footprints until their 3D bodies are implemented. The registry coverage test passes with the released dependency.

The broader local suite reports failures in the ball-bearing preservation hash and renderer-discovery tests. Both reproduce on the unmodified base commit. The GitHub preview workflow passed. The separate Vercel deployment failed during npm dependency resolution for React and react-reconciler.

title: perf: reduce async overhead in SPICE simulations
description: Reduces asynchronous overhead in SPICE simulations by modifying input handling to improve performance without changing the public Simulation API or numerical solver.
body:
The TPS54320 benchmark spends avoidable time in Asyncify-instrumented numerical callbacks. Input suspension was injected into the general command dispatcher, so conservative indirect-call handling also instrumented solver paths.

Stacked on #13. Move input suspension to the top-level command loop and return a Promise from the existing internal handler. Numerical callbacks can then remain synchronous. The setjmp trampoline stays explicitly marked as asynchronous. The public Simulation API and numerical solver are unchanged.

The boundary test keeps a 10-second watchdog active through startup and simulation and requires a positive input count with one pause per input. Bridge declarations describe the asynchronous handler and command-string getter. The npm workflow builds and copies the patched WASM before bundling, runs the boundary regression before publishing, and explicitly selects npm for the `@tscircuit` scope.

| Reproduction | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Three-command `.control` block | 9 handler pauses / 6 inputs | 6 pauses / 6 inputs |
| TPS54320, first 50 µs, three paired runs | 6.11–6.26 s | 4.47–4.48 s |
| TPS54320, first 500 µs | 112.60 s | 83.25 s |

The 500 µs benchmark is about **26% faster**. All **194,298 raw timestamps and VOUT samples are bit-for-bit identical**. The startup SVG from #13 remains identical, as expected for a runtime improvement. Component values, model, transient settings and tolerances were not altered.

Validation: build, ESLint, TypeScript, patch application, source/package regressions, GF180, noise/AC switching, module reuse, fatal-error rejection, strict TI startup, transient numerical checks, existing/new SVG regressions, and the Chromium browser regression pass. Chromium used the already-installed executable through a temporary local config; Firefox/WebKit were not rerun.

Test guard verification:

| Injected condition | Previous test | Updated test |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Healthy bridge | Exit 0, 6 pauses / 6 inputs | Exit 0, 6 pauses / 6 inputs |
| Startup never resolves | Exit 0 before assertions | Exit 1, watchdog |
| Simulation never resolves | Exit 0 before assertions | Exit 1, watchdog |
| Input bridge never resolves | Exit 0 before assertions | Exit 1, watchdog |
| No external commands consumed | Exit 0, 0 pauses / 0 inputs | Exit 1, assertion |

Release validation: a fresh Docker WASM build, frozen Bun install from tracked manifests, boundary tests against fresh source and built package artifacts, source/package regressions (including strict TI startup and module reuse), ESLint, TypeScript, and actionlint pass. npm dry runs confirm the workflow scope selects npmjs.org instead of the package's default GitHub registry.

The full `npm test` command reaches the existing missing `test/fixtures/figure-10-17/tps63802-pfm-buck.cir` fixture and stops there. The fixture is also absent from main. Chromium was run separately.

**Scope:** this removes measured overhead. The full 10 ms TI run has not been benchmarked with this fix, and full-model runtime remains expensive.

title: fix: recognize PSpice VALUE= boolean expressions
description: Fixes incorrect output behavior in ngspice for boolean expressions using VALUE syntax, aligning with TIs XOR rule for the TPS8208485 models.
body:
TI's TPS82084/85 models contain an XOR rule: **the output should be ON when exactly one input is ON.**

title: Warn on explicit undefined in function signatures across repositories
description: Adds an advisory warning for TypeScript function annotations that explicitly accept or return undefined, encouraging better handling of absence at the caller level.
body:
## Rule

`handbook/review-undefined-signature` is an advisory, cross-repository warning. It flags added TypeScript annotations that explicitly accept or return `undefined`, including inline parameter fields and promise results. It does not flag plain optional `?` parameters, standalone stored-data types, or inferred types.

The warning recommends handling absence at the caller when the callee needs a value, and keeping expected absence separate from real failure. Lookups returning no result remain valid. This supersedes the narrow Core-only route-length error originally proposed here.

Inspired by [Shibo’s review on Core #5888](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5888#discussion_r4691819133).
